name: B10-0152/2024 – Motion for a resolution (as a whole)
title: MOTION FOR A RESOLUTION on the draft Commission Implementing Decision authorising the placing on the market of products containing, consisting of or produced from genetically modified maize DP202216, pursuant to Regulation (EC) No 1829/2003 of the European Parliament and of the Council
part_text:
The European Parliament is asking the European Commission to withdraw its plan to allow imports of a genetically modified maize, called DP202216, for food and feed. The maize is engineered to survive spraying with glufosinate, a weedkiller banned in the EU since 2018. Parliament says the weedkiller risks were never properly assessed, that member states never backed the plan, and that approving it would contradict the EU's environmental promises. The resolution is an objection, not a law change.

- **What changes:** Nothing yet. Parliament formally objects and asks the Commission to withdraw the plan and send a new draft.
- **Who it affects:** Farmers, food and feed importers, and consumers, if the maize is approved.
- **What happens next:** The Commission decides whether to withdraw, change or keep its plan; Parliament cannot block it alone.
